result.title: Controlled One-Click Benchmarking and Post-Fusion Recalibration for Support-Conditioned Medical Segmentation
result.comment: Accepted at the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2026)
result.summary: Sparse-prompt medical segmentation is hard to compare when prompts, supports, thresholds, and splits differ. This paper uses a controlled one-click protocol: each test image receives one positive foreground click, training-only support, validation-only checkpoint selection, and no test-time threshold tuning. We propose {Support-Aware Recalibration (SAR)}, a late post-fusion recalibration block for MultiverSeg that combines large-kernel spatial gating with squeeze-and-excitation channel recalibration after support--query fusion. BUSI, NerveUS-BP-present, and Kvasir-SEG are evaluated with matched 697 foreground-present sample budgets, shared splits/clicks, and threshold-free Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC. Compared with a protocol-matched raw-support MultiverSeg baseline, the main SAR configuration shows favorable mean Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC performance on BUSI, NerveUS-BP-present, and Kvasir-SEG, while reducing logged training time in this implementation. These controlled results indicate that late post-fusion recalibration is useful under a leakage-controlled one-click protocol.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在受控「一键」协议下比较稀疏提示医学分割，并提出 Support-Aware Recalibration（SAR）：在 MultiverSeg 的 support–query 融合后加入大核空间门控与通道重校准，用阈值无关的 Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC 在三个数据集上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其融合后的空间/通道门控重校准可能为 LVR 中视觉证据加权与筛选提供机制线索，但论文不涉及 latent 推理状态、动态计算或停止决策，与主线距离较远，可供核查其门控是否可迁移。
